title: Basic Pitch: a real upload gets real notes — live (PR-37)
path: synthesised melodic song -> upload -> analysis with BASIC_PITCH configured -> Song Model melody/bass notes
song: the same synthesised song the Definition-of-Done run used, whose Song Model held 0 chords and 0 melody notes
observations: Before this change a FULL_SONG was never sent to Basic Pitch at all: transcription ran only for VOCAL_ONLY and SOLO_INSTRUMENT sources, which is why the Definition-of-Done Song Model carried 0 chords and 0 melody notes.

BASIC_PITCH now appears in providerProvenance for a FULL_SONG at all, which is the fix: the provider is asked. Before this change it was never scheduled for a full mix and therefore never even reported as absent.

No notes came back in this run, and the reason is transport, not the provider: the deployed worker refuses any source URL that does not resolve to a global address (its SSRF guard), and this development API serves signed URLs from PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5000. A cloud worker cannot reach a local object store. The worker is right to refuse; the run records HTTP 400 rather than pretending.

What is proven here: the endpoint exists, is healthy, and passes the full identity gate (pinned package tree, pinned checkpoint tree b74344cd..., pinned runtime, build-time smoke, Apache-2.0). What is not: notes in a Song Model, which needs the API reachable from the worker.

Basic Pitch would run on the mix here in any case. Upstream recommends one instrument at a time, so stem-by-stem transcription (Demucs -> Basic Pitch per stem) will be better; that needs the Demucs endpoint and is not this change.
